extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (AP audience); policymakers and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service (AP) international and national news reporting covering diplomacy, politics, military incidents, and technical government programs (e.g., AEC tests). Articles provide factual accounts, quotes from officials, and background context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radiation exposure limits for test workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Test workers try to keep their exposure under 3.9 roentgens in a 13-week period. A dose of three-tenths roentgen per week has been accepted by [authorities].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article gives these numeric limits as the operational target for on-site personnel and contrasts them with measured fallout values (most outside the test area are in milliroentgens). It is presented as the AEC's occupational-exposure practice during the Nevada series.

rubrics_metrics.name: General-public radiation safety guideline (AEC)
rubrics_metrics.description: For general public safety outside the test area, the AEC has established a guide ... cited in the article in connection with allowable exposure and monitoring (text references the figure '3.9 roentgens' in relation to public safety and an annual guide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding text explains that monitoring stations and public warnings are intended to keep communities well below allowable doses; the article reports the AEC's stated numerical guides though the prose is fragmented—context: public-safety limits and monitoring thresholds for fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallout-minimizing test design (fireball height and tower use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests will 'keep the atomic fireballs farther from the ground' to decrease the amount of dirt sucked up and made radioactive; the use of 500-foot towers in at least four shots is planned to cut heavy fallout to a minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article explains the rationale: higher bursts reduce local fallout by limiting ground material vaporized into the cloud. This is presented as a safety/technical design choice to reduce off-site contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and public-notification protocol for tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve monitoring stations have been established within a 200-mile area of the test site to warn residents of possible radiation fallout; thousands of explanatory booklets have been printed and distributed by the AEC to townspeople and school children in likely-path areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AEC's precautions include establishing monitoring networks, public information campaigns, printed booklets, invitations to select civilian observers (governors, city officials, industry representatives, press), and warnings to residents (e.g., previous advisories to stay indoors). The article also notes that newsmen will not be allowed on the site for safety/operational reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational protocol: 'optional two-in-one' shot
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'optional' two-in-one shot will be set up: two shots prepared for the same day and, depending on the weather, one of them will be detonated—if the weather is very good the tougher device will be set off; if not, the less difficult shot will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as an operational decision rule to permit choice of device based on weather conditions to manage fallout and test objectives; presented as a new gimmick devised by AEC scientists for the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on maximum shot yield in the series
rubrics_metrics.description: AEC says 'there will be no shot bigger than any in the last Nevada series in spring 1953.' The highest yield explosion in that prior series was 'considerably less than 100 kilotons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reassure about relative scale of forthcoming detonations and as part of safety framing—combined with other measures (tower shots, monitoring) to limit fallout and risk to nearby communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and functional limits of South Viet Nam provisional assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisional assembly will include representatives of premier's cabinet and spokesmen for all classes, parties and sects (including nearly 700,000 refugees); it will not be able to pass laws or unseat cabinets. Its chief function will be to give the government a broader base by examining the budget and consulting with officials on various measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article specifies selection/election mechanics (200 members elected by provincial and municipal councils rather than directly), the provisional body's symbolic role to broaden support, and expectations about later general elections and constitutional drafting. This is described as the design and legal/functional constraints of the provisional body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armistice prohibition on introduction of new weapons into Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions in the armistice agreement prohibit the introduction into North or South Korea of any new weapons other than for replacement of worn-out material already there; accumulation of jet fighters in North Korea since the armistice is noted as strictly forbidden by the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the legal standard invoked when discussing claims about MIG fighter origins and whether their presence would constitute an armistice violation; used to frame diplomatic/official responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for diplomatic protest about air incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials said they were hamstrung by a lack of detailed information and had been unable to make out the kind of case suitable for a protest to a Communist government; substantial evidence of national markings on the planes appeared to be missing, possibly because the brief fight occurred at high speeds and emblems were not clearly seen or photographed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article implies a practical evidentiary standard for lodging formal diplomatic protests: sufficient, identifiable evidence (national markings, clear photographs or other corroboration) is required before making a protest to another government.
